title: Dyslipidaemia and cardiovascular risk (India)
specialty: Cardiology / Internal Medicine / Endocrinology / Primary Care

evidenceAudit.scope: Lipid testing, cardiovascular risk categories, LDL-cholesterol and non-HDL targets, statins, ezetimibe, PCSK9 inhibitors, inclisiran and management of hypertriglyceridaemia in Indian adults, built on the Cardiological Society of India (CSI) clinical practice guidelines for dyslipidaemia (2024).
findings: Risk categories (low, moderate, high, very high, extremely high), LDL-C targets (below 100, 100, 70 and 55 mg/dL) and non-HDL targets (below 130, 130, 100, 85 mg/dL), triglyceride below 150 and Lp(a) below 50 mg/dL, statin intensity doses (atorvastatin 40–80 mg high, 10–20 mg moderate; rosuvastatin 20–40 mg high, 5–10 mg moderate), ezetimibe 10 mg with statin early after acute coronary syndrome (ACS), non-statin therapy if LDL-C not below 55 mg/dL at 4 weeks, evolocumab 140 mg every 2 weeks or 420 mg monthly, inclisiran 284 mg at day 1, day 90 then 6-monthly, fenofibrate 145 mg for triglycerides above 500 mg/dL, icosapent ethyl 2 g twice daily, non-fasting lipid testing, lipid profile by age 18 and Lp(a) once checked against the CSI dyslipidaemia guideline executive summary (Indian Heart J 2024).

Bempedoic acid 180 mg once daily with maximally tolerated statin, no adjustment at eGFR 30 or above or in Child-Pugh A or B, and hyperuricaemia and tendon warnings checked against the Drugs.com dosage monograph (US label).
unverifiedSections: CSI gives no routine adult interval for repeat lipid testing and no CK threshold (section 5.1 advises against routine muscle and liver enzyme monitoring); the 4–12 week recheck and yearly review shown are general practice.
The extremely high-risk group has no numeric target in Table 1 of the executive summary; it is treated as at least the very high-risk target here.
The CSI summary notes South Asians may respond to lower statin doses (section 5.1); the US label suggests starting rosuvastatin at 5 mg in Asian patients.
Drug cautions, contraindications and renal or hepatic adjustment lines without a source tag are general pharmacology statements and need formulary confirmation.

pathophysiology.summary: Indians develop coronary artery disease about a decade earlier than many other populations, with atherogenic dyslipidaemia (high triglycerides, low HDL, small dense LDL) and high Lp(a). The CSI guideline asks for a lipid profile in everyone by 18 years (non-fasting is acceptable), Lp(a) once in a lifetime, risk categorisation by risk factors and established disease, and LDL-C targets that fall as risk rises — down to below 55 mg/dL in very high-risk patients. High-intensity statins are the foundation; ezetimibe, then PCSK9 inhibitors or inclisiran, are added when targets are not met. Very high triglycerides (above 500 mg/dL) are treated to prevent pancreatitis. Because risk is cumulative, the earlier and lower LDL-C is brought down, the larger the benefit; the CSI therefore asks for a first lipid profile by age 18 and cascade testing in families with premature disease.
keyMechanisms: LDL particles enter the artery wall and drive atherosclerosis; lowering LDL reduces events in proportion.
Statins inhibit HMG-CoA reductase; ezetimibe blocks intestinal cholesterol absorption; PCSK9 inhibitors increase LDL receptor recycling.
Lp(a) is inherited and independently causes coronary disease.
Very high triglycerides cause acute pancreatitis.

symptoms: Premature coronary disease in patient or family
Exertional chest pain or claudication in established atherosclerosis
Abdominal pain (pancreatitis) with very high triglycerides
physicalSigns: Tendon xanthomas on the Achilles tendon or knuckles (familial hypercholesterolaemia)
Signs of secondary causes: obesity, acanthosis, hypothyroid features, oedema
redFlags: LDL-C 190 mg/dL or more or tendon xanthomas: suspect familial hypercholesterolaemia
Muscle pain with dark urine on statin: check CK
Premature coronary disease in family: cascade testing (CSI)

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Hypothyroidism, nephrotic syndrome, cholestasis, uncontrolled diabetes or drugs; TSH, urine protein, liver tests and HbA1c settle it before starting lifelong treatment.
Very high LDL-C, tendon xanthomas and premature coronary disease in relatives; family screening and genetic testing settle it (CSI).
Triglycerides above 1000 mg/dL from childhood with recurrent pancreatitis; specialist lipid testing settles it.
Premature disease despite normal LDL-C; a single Lp(a) measurement above 50 mg/dL settles it (CSI).

differentials.condition: Laboratory artefact from non-fasting or lipaemic sample
differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Isolated triglyceride rise after a heavy meal; a repeat sample settles it, though non-fasting testing is acceptable for risk estimation (CSI).

differentials.condition: Statin-associated muscle symptoms versus other myopathy
differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Aches with normal CK versus weakness with raised CK or hypothyroidism; CK and TSH settle it.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: One risk factor: tobacco, hypertension, diabetes or premature family history.
Two or more risk factors, CKD, diabetes over 10 years, or heterozygous FH.
Clinical ASCVD (coronary or other vascular beds), diabetes over 20 years, heterozygous FH with ASCVD, or a lesion over 50% in 2 coronary vessels on imaging.
Recurrent vascular events, or ASCVD with a genetic dyslipidaemia (FH or high Lp(a)); no separate numeric target in Table 1 — use at least the very high-risk target.
Low and moderate below 100; high below 70; very high below 55 mg/dL.

diagnosticCriteria.criterion: Other targets for all groups (CSI Table 1)
diagnosticCriteria.threshold: HDL-C above 40 mg/dL (men) and 50 mg/dL (women); triglycerides below 150 mg/dL; Lp(a) below 50 mg/dL.
LDL-C 190 mg/dL or more on repeat testing: start a statin.

clinicalManagement.title: Assess risk
actions: Lipid profile (non-fasting acceptable), Lp(a) once, and screen for secondary causes (CSI).
Place the person in a CSI risk category and set the LDL-C and non-HDL-C targets (CSI Figure 2, Table 1).

clinicalManagement.title: Lifestyle
actions: Diet with fewer refined carbohydrates and fried foods and more vegetables, pulses and whole grains (CSI Table 4).
Regular exercise, weight control, stop tobacco in all forms, limit alcohol.

clinicalManagement.title: Statin
clinicalManagement.timeframe: From diagnosis in high and very high risk
actions: High-intensity statin for high and very high risk (CSI Table 2).
After ACS: add ezetimibe at the start; LDL-C below 55 mg/dL as early as possible (CSI 4.1).
LDL-C 190 mg/dL or more on repeat testing: start a statin even without other risk factors (CSI 9.2).

clinicalManagement.title: Intensify
actions: Not at target on maximally tolerated statin: add ezetimibe 10 mg (CSI).
High or very high risk still above target: PCSK9 inhibitor or inclisiran, used mainly in very high risk (CSI 5.4).
After ACS, LDL-C not below 55 mg/dL at 4 weeks: add bempedoic acid, a PCSK9 inhibitor or inclisiran (CSI 4.1).

clinicalManagement.title: Triglycerides
actions: Above 500 mg/dL: fenofibrate to prevent pancreatitis (CSI).
Still raised after lifestyle and diabetes control in ASCVD or diabetes aged 40 or older: consider icosapent ethyl (CSI 6).

clinicalManagement.title: Monitor and support adherence
actions: Repeat lipids 4 weeks after ACS (CSI 4.1); otherwise 4–12 weeks after starting or changing treatment, then yearly (general practice).
Muscle symptoms: check CK and TSH; retry a lower dose or another statin rather than stopping lipid lowering.

vignette.text: Mr P, a 44-year-old software engineer from Bengaluru, comes for a health check. His father had a heart attack at 48. He does not smoke, BP is 128/82 mmHg and HbA1c 5.6%. Total cholesterol is 312 mg/dL, LDL-C 228 mg/dL, HDL-C 42 mg/dL and triglycerides 140 mg/dL. You notice thickened Achilles tendons. He asks whether diet alone will fix it.

guidedApproach.title: Why LDL-C is the main target
guidedApproach.prompt: Why do guidelines focus on LDL-C and set lower targets for higher risk?
guidedApproach.guidance: Atherosclerosis begins when apolipoprotein B-containing particles, mainly LDL, enter the arterial wall and are retained and oxidised, attracting macrophages that form foam cells and plaques. The amount of plaque reflects both the LDL-C level and how long the artery has been exposed, so a person with familial hypercholesterolaemia carries a decade's extra exposure by middle age. Trials of statins, ezetimibe and PCSK9 inhibitors all show that lowering LDL-C reduces events in proportion to the fall, without a clear lower threshold — hence the targets fall from below 100 to below 55 mg/dL as risk rises. Indians often have atherogenic dyslipidaemia with high triglycerides and low HDL-C, and about one in four South Asians has a raised Lp(a), which is inherited and not lowered by lifestyle.

guidedApproach.title: Spotting the high-risk patient
guidedApproach.prompt: Who needs more than a routine check?
guidedApproach.guidance: Most people with dyslipidaemia have no symptoms, so the diagnosis is made by testing and by recognising risk. Ask about premature coronary disease in first-degree relatives (men under 55, women under 60), smoking or tobacco chewing, hypertension and diabetes and its duration. Examine for tendon xanthomas, xanthelasma and corneal arcus at a young age, which suggest familial hypercholesterolaemia, and for eruptive xanthomas with very high triglycerides. Look for secondary causes — hypothyroidism, nephrotic syndrome, cholestasis, poorly controlled diabetes and drugs such as steroids — because treating them can correct the lipids.

guidedApproach.title: What to measure and when
guidedApproach.prompt: Which tests does the CSI recommend?
guidedApproach.guidance: A standard lipid profile (total cholesterol, LDL-C, HDL-C, non-HDL-C and triglycerides) can be taken non-fasting for risk estimation and treatment decisions. Everyone should have a profile by age 18, and Lp(a) should be measured at least once in a lifetime; a value above 50 mg/dL marks extra inherited risk. Check TSH, glucose or HbA1c, creatinine, liver tests and urine protein to exclude secondary causes before starting lifelong treatment. After starting or changing therapy, repeat the lipids at 4–12 weeks to confirm the target is met, then yearly. Check CK and TSH if muscle symptoms appear. Cascade testing of relatives is advised in familial hypercholesterolaemia and premature coronary disease.

guidedApproach.title: Statins first, then add-ons
guidedApproach.prompt: How do you reach the target?
guidedApproach.guidance: Lifestyle change matters for everyone but rarely reaches targets alone in high-risk patients. The CSI places people in risk categories and sets LDL-C targets of below 100, 70 or 55 mg/dL. High and very high-risk patients start a high-intensity statin — atorvastatin 40–80 mg or rosuvastatin 20–40 mg — and South Asians may respond well to lower doses. After an acute coronary syndrome, ezetimibe is added from the start. If the target is not met at 4–12 weeks, add ezetimibe 10 mg, then a PCSK9 inhibitor or inclisiran in very high-risk patients. Triglycerides above 500 mg/dL need fenofibrate to prevent pancreatitis; for persistently raised triglycerides in ASCVD or diabetes, icosapent ethyl reduces events. Statin side effects are usually manageable with a dose or drug change rather than stopping.

boardQuestions.vignette: A 44-year-old man has LDL-C 228 mg/dL, thickened Achilles tendons and a father with myocardial infarction at 48. He does not smoke, is not diabetic and has normal BP. TSH and urine protein are normal. He has no symptoms of coronary disease.
boardQuestions.question: What is the most appropriate management?

options.text: Diet alone for 6 months, then recheck
options.explanation: Familial hypercholesterolaemia rarely responds adequately to diet; delay prolongs exposure.
Fibrates lower triglycerides; his problem is very high LDL-C.

options.text: High-intensity statin with family screening, adding ezetimibe if LDL-C stays above 70 mg/dL
options.explanation: Correct. Heterozygous FH is a high-risk category (CSI): LDL-C target below 70 mg/dL, with cascade testing of relatives.
Icosapent ethyl is for raised triglycerides in ASCVD or diabetes.

options.text: No treatment because he has no symptoms
options.explanation: Risk is driven by lifetime LDL exposure, not symptoms.

boardQuestions.educationalObjective: Recognise familial hypercholesterolaemia and treat to a high-risk target.
boardQuestions.keyPoint: Tendon xanthomas + LDL-C above 190 mg/dL: think FH; statin, target below 70, screen family.

boardQuestions.vignette: A 58-year-old woman had an NSTEMI treated with a stent 6 weeks ago and has taken atorvastatin 80 mg daily with good adherence since discharge. She has hypertension and no diabetes. Her LDL-C today is 82 mg/dL, HDL-C 38 mg/dL and triglycerides 160 mg/dL, and she has no muscle symptoms.
boardQuestions.question: What is the best next step?

options.explanation: She is very high risk with LDL-C above the target of 55 mg/dL (CSI).

Correct. Very high risk needs LDL-C below 55 mg/dL and after ACS ezetimibe is added to the statin. Ezetimibe alone may not give the 33% further fall needed, so recheck at 4 weeks and add bempedoic acid, a PCSK9 inhibitor or inclisiran if not at target (CSI 4.1).
This is a moderate-intensity dose and would raise LDL-C.
Triglycerides are only mildly raised; fibrates have no role at 150–499 mg/dL (CSI).

options.text: Stop the statin and start evolocumab alone
options.explanation: PCSK9 inhibitors are added to, not substituted for, maximally tolerated statin therapy.

boardQuestions.educationalObjective: Intensify lipid lowering after acute coronary syndrome.
boardQuestions.keyPoint: Very high risk: LDL-C below 55 mg/dL; add ezetimibe early.

boardQuestions.vignette: A 40-year-old man with type 2 diabetes and heavy alcohol use presents with epigastric pain radiating to the back. Serum lipase is three times normal and fasting triglycerides are 1450 mg/dL. LDL-C cannot be calculated. He is not on any lipid-lowering drug.
boardQuestions.question: Which long-term lipid treatment is most important after he recovers?

options.explanation: Statins alone do not adequately lower triglycerides of this level, although as a man with diabetes aged 40 he also qualifies for a statin once triglycerides fall.
Icosapent ethyl reduces cardiovascular events but is not the main drug to prevent pancreatitis at triglycerides above 500 mg/dL.
Triglycerides above 500 mg/dL carry a high pancreatitis risk and need treatment (CSI).

options.text: Fenofibrate 145 mg daily, alcohol abstinence and glucose control
options.explanation: Correct. Fasting triglycerides above 500 mg/dL are the clearest indication for fenofibrate to prevent pancreatitis (CSI), with control of secondary causes.
Ezetimibe mainly lowers LDL-C and does little for triglycerides of this level.

boardQuestions.keyPoint: Triglycerides above 500 mg/dL: fenofibrate plus correction of alcohol and glucose.

patientEducation: Statins are lifelong; report muscle pain with dark urine.
Diet: less refined carbohydrate and fried food; more vegetables and pulses.
lifestyleAndDiet: Regular exercise, weight loss, stop tobacco, limit alcohol.

algorithms.title: Lipid management by CSI risk category

nodes.text: Clinical ASCVD (any vascular bed), diabetes over 20 years, FH with ASCVD, or over 50% lesion in 2 coronary vessels?
High-intensity statin (atorvastatin 40–80 or rosuvastatin 20–40); target LDL-C below 55 mg/dL
Add ezetimibe from the start; if LDL-C not below 55 mg/dL at 4 weeks add bempedoic acid, a PCSK9 inhibitor or inclisiran
LDL-C below 55 mg/dL at recheck (4 weeks after ACS)?
Add ezetimibe 10 mg; then PCSK9 inhibitor or inclisiran if still above target
Two or more risk factors, CKD, diabetes over 10 years or heterozygous FH?
High-intensity statin; LDL-C below 70 mg/dL; add ezetimibe if not at target
One risk factor (tobacco, hypertension, diabetes, premature family history)?
Lifestyle, then statin if LDL-C stays at or above 100 mg/dL
LDL-C 190 mg/dL or more on repeat testing?
Start a statin; assess for familial hypercholesterolaemia
Lifestyle; LDL-C target below 100 mg/dL; recheck periodically
